title: Residency SKU bundling and pricing experiment for regulated verticals
creator: Ethan Morales
description: Experiment and playbook to offer pre-bundled residency SKUs tailored for regulated industries (finance, health, government) that combine: explicit EU/UK SCC enforcement, retention limits, curated subprocessor lists, and a pricing delta. Goal is to validate packaging that simplifies enterprise procurement and reduces legal review time while preserving predictable unit economics for Redwood.
background: Sales and legal teams report long sales cycles where customers repeatedly request bespoke residency language and subprocessor attestation. We currently surface these as ad-hoc contract amendments or expensive private deployments. This experiment aims to productize common asks into a small set of standard SKUs to reduce negotiation friction and enable self-serve upgrades.
success_metrics: Reduce average legal negotiation time for targeted segment from 28 days to <=10 days
>20% of inbound regulated RFIs choose a residency SKU instead of bespoke contract within Q1 post-launch
Maintain <10% incremental per-token latency and <15% cost premium for SKU variants versus baseline hosted API
SLA and audit checklist accepted by 3 reference customers in pilot cohort
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 SKU tiers (Standard, Enhanced, Isolated) with specific retention windows and subprocessor commitments
Create contract annex language templates (EU/UK SCC activation, retention schedules) reviewed and approved by Legal
Pricing matrix with clear unit economics and list-price multipliers validated with Finance
Console UI flow to select residency SKU during billing/checkout and expose SKU terms in customer portal
Pilot onboarding run with at least two sales opportunities and documented customer feedback
deliverables: Contract annex templates and quick-start Q&A for sales
Pricing sheet and revenue model impact analysis
Console selection UI mockups and acceptance criteria
Pilot onboarding checklist and post-pilot report
decisions: Use SCCs activation flag per-customer (opt-in) rather than creating full legal variation per region
Expose fixed retention windows (30d / 90d / custom on Dedicated only) instead of open-ended retention options
Bundle a vetted subprocessor list per SKU; customers can request additional subprocessors via Contract Addendum process
Price as percentage uplift over baseline hosted rates rather than absolute per-token price to simplify comparisons
tradeoffs: Standard SKUs simplify sales but may not cover edge regulatory requirements, requiring fallback to Private deployments
Tighter retention windows reduce legal risk but can increase caching inefficiencies and cost per token
Offering explicit subprocessor lists reduces negotiation time but increases maintenance overhead for compliance team
risks: Legal review finds SCC activation model insufficient for some enterprise counsel
Engineering complexity to enforce retention windows and subprocessor filtering across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
Pricing uplift could materially reduce conversion if not aligned with perceived value
Potential operational strain on onboarding for customers requesting rapid SCC activation
